cards.headline: Vivaldi with 75% thrown away
cards.snippet: For his 2012 album Recomposed by Max Richter: Vivaldi – The Four Seasons, which includes Spring 1, the German-born British composer Max Richter reworked Vivaldi's famous score. He said he threw out about 75% of Vivaldi's original material. The parts he kept are phased and looped, which shows his grounding in minimalist and postmodern music. One critic joked that Richter might be called a baroque decomposer. The album topped the iTunes classical chart in the UK, Germany and the US.
cards.context: Spring 1 comes from Recomposed by Max Richter: Vivaldi – The Four Seasons (2012).

cards.headline: Edits he called 'jump cuts'
cards.snippet: In his 2012 recomposition of Vivaldi's The Four Seasons, Max Richter reworked the music in several ways. He changed the tempo, made the rhythm less regimented than Vivaldi's, specified particular dynamics and altered the instrumentation. In Spring 2, for example, a viola became a cello. He also called the musical breaks in the work "jump cuts", a cinematic term. In his description, they create leaps, or the sense of a trap-door opening.
cards.context: He also changed tempo, rhythm and instrumentation across the four seasons.

cards.headline: A brain tumour, then a new career
cards.snippet: I had a brain tumour removed and once I was back on my feet this piece of music gave me the courage to quit my job and follow my passion to become a film maker.
cards.context: A life-changing story from a listener.

cards.headline: Live at Pukkelpop 2018 with a string orchestra and violin soloist
cards.snippet: Recorded live at Pukkelpop festival on 16 August 2018, with the Marquee String Orchestra conducted by Jef Neve and Peter Bogaert as violin soloist, playing Richter's Recomposed take on Vivaldi. One listener: "the conductor's smile was so precious"
